conclusions: The exact target is every URep field at each supplied original normalized coefficient curve. NP.span supplies split nonisomorphic absolute irreducibility of the one or two residual blocks; it is not inferred merely from the original residual characters.

Topological finite generation makes continuous cocycles into each finite residual adjoint module finite. Wang-Erickson Proposition 3.6 therefore supplies the finite continuous Cayley-Hamilton algebra and the equivalent topologies; its use does not require ell>n.

The relation ideal is in the trace radical by the actual Pair and auxiliary equations. In the original distinct-character GMA, every primitive corner has trace one; hence every diagonal corner of that ideal is zero. The cycle formula in Proposition 2.23 proves descent of the full determinant after arbitrary coefficient extension, without division by n!.

P.ker is D.chBar(P.gens), not P.gens. The source closure is the intersection of the coefficient-power and open-normal-subgroup relation ideals. In the finite completed quotient, the dense B-submodule image of B[G] is closed, hence surjective, with precisely that algebraic kernel. Right exactness gives Hat.ker as the literal algebraic span of the image of the already-closed P.ker after completion at the curve; no second closure, saturation or torsion removal is inserted.

The specified curve variable and coefficient residue field make f:B->k[[t]] surjective: its compact image is closed and contains the polynomials. The completed local ring has residue field exactly k((t)).

The semisimple quotient of the full special fibre has the prescribed matrix blocks; the full fibre radical and N/mN remain. Finite completeness makes radical-adic and coefficient-adic topologies equivalent.

The actual identity polarization induces transpose in each block, not block exchange or a symplectic sign. Self-adjoint primitive idempotents lift by the displayed Newton iteration; transpose-compatible matrix units lift by Hensel square roots of units in 1+m, using only 2 invertible.

Rank-one Cayley-Hamilton corners equal R and have trace one. Star makes b symmetric, cyclic trace identifies both products, and associativity gives b(m,n)p=b(n,p)m. Thus R direct_sum N has the claimed commutative associative multiplication with N squared in m. Symmetry alone would not suffice.

The block embedding preserves all products and its canonical cycle determinant is the full original determinant. It respects the original residual basis and polarization and retains every annihilator-torsion element of N.

If an element of Ann(N) lies outside Q, N vanishes over every coefficient field with kernel Q. The exact original equation algebra then becomes a product of full matrix algebras, contradicting the original NonSS witness. This uses the proved exact kernel, not an arbitrary faithful representation.
The image of the finite original B-algebra is the required finite B-submodule P. Its multiplicative stability and continuity give the actual all-j, all-g open-normal-subgroup condition.

The trace discriminant implication follows from the rank bound a^2+(n-a)^2<n^2 when the odd-square ideal vanishes. It creates no numerical annihilator bound, patched support, nonzero automorphic seed or two-sided global rigidity.
